industry_analysis.culture: Car culture varies by region (American muscle/trucks, European luxury/performance, Japanese reliability/efficiency). Aftermarket customization popular in US, Japan, Middle East. Brand loyalty strong among enthusiasts.
industry_analysis.consumer: Quality and reliability critical for safety-critical components. Price competition from aftermarket vs. OEM suppliers. Online parts lookup (VIN-based) and ordering growing. Professional installers prefer known brands.
industry_analysis.infra: IATF 16949 quality management mandatory for OEM supply. OEM specifications and PPAP approvals required. Just-in-time delivery to assembly plants. Global supply chain with tier 1/2/3 structure.
industry_analysis.population: Vehicle parc size (total registered vehicles) drives aftermarket demand. EV transition fundamentally affecting parts demand profiles. Aging vehicle population increases repair and replacement needs.
industry_analysis.social: Right-to-repair legislation expanding. Vehicle customization and modification culture. Car sharing and mobility-as-a-service. Autonomous vehicle development reshaping future parts demand.
industry_analysis.environment: Emissions regulations driving technology changes (Euro 7, China 6). EV transition eliminating ICE-specific parts. Lightweight materials for fuel efficiency. End-of-life vehicle recycling regulations (ELV Directive).
industry_analysis.opportunity: EV components and charging infrastructure. Connected car technologies and ADAS sensors. Aftermarket growth for aging vehicle fleets. Emerging market vehicle ownership growth.

compliance_summary: IATF 16949, OEM specifications, ECE regulations, DOT standards (US), emissions compliance, PPAP documentation.
